tracks.narration: Two transformations, two orders. Does it matter which one you do first?
Take matrix A — a rotation by forty-five degrees. And matrix B — a stretch along x, a squeeze along y.
Apply B first — the unit square stretches and squashes. Then apply A — the deformed square rotates. The single matrix A B captures both steps at once.
Now swap the order. Apply A first, then B. The square rotates, then stretches — and lands somewhere different. The matrix B A is not the same as A B.
A B means B first, then A — A acts last on whatever B produced. And in general, A B does not equal B A.
